instructions.task: Read the Craigslist listing and the buyer-seller chat. After the chat the buyer submits a formal offer and the seller accepts or rejects it. Decide how the chat ended.
notes: Acceptance is often informal: 'ok', 'fair enough', 'I'll take it', 'sounds good', 'deal', 'that works', or simply moving on to pickup or payment after a price was named.
A seller saying 'X and you have a deal' counts as agreement if the buyer was already willing to pay X or responds positively.
A buyer saying they want to buy at the listed price, with no objection from the seller, counts as agreement.
A low offer from the buyer that the seller never answered or accepted is not an agreement.

If the seller's last word on price is a number they say they will sell for (a counteroffer, 'X is the lowest I'll go', 'make it X and it's a deal') and the buyer did not reject it, the buyer can simply offer that price: classify as seller_named_final_price.

criteria.agreed_price: Both sides accepted the same price, formally or informally, and nobody backed out afterwards.
criteria.agreed_then_logistics: A price was accepted (possibly implicitly) and the chat moved on to pickup, delivery, payment, paperwork or submitting the offer.
criteria.buyer_accepts_seller_terms: The buyer accepted the seller's last price or terms, even with odd wording (e.g. 'fair enough', 'I'll take it', 'today works').
criteria.pending_offer: The chat ends with the buyer's offer or request for a lower price that the seller did not accept or answer.
criteria.refused_or_walked_away: One side rejected the last price or ended the negotiation without agreement.
criteria.never_negotiated: The chat stops before any real negotiation: greetings, item questions only, or a single message.
criteria.nonsense: The chat is gibberish, about a different item, or the participants are not seriously negotiating.
criteria.seller_named_final_price: The seller's last price message names a price they are willing to sell for (counteroffer, lowest price, conditional deal), and the buyer did not reject it afterwards.

instructions.task: Craigslist negotiation chat. After the chat the buyer submits a formal offer and the seller accepts or rejects it. Look at the last few messages. Is there a price that the seller has said they will accept and that the buyer has not rejected?
notes: It does not matter who spoke last. If the seller named a final price and the buyer replied 'I'll take it', 'fair enough', 'ok', 'today works' or similar, both have accepted that price.
If the buyer offered a price and the seller replied positively or moved on to arranging pickup, both have accepted that price.
If the last message is the buyer's lower offer or a request to go lower that the seller never accepted, there is no price the seller has accepted.

If the seller's last message names the price they will sell for (a counteroffer, 'X is my lowest', 'make it X and you have a deal') and the buyer did not reject it, the buyer can simply offer that price: answer yes_seller_final_price.

criteria.yes_mutual_price: Yes: both buyer and seller stated or accepted the same price, and neither withdrew.
criteria.yes_seller_final_price: Yes: the seller's last price message names a price they will sell for, and the buyer has not rejected it.
criteria.no_buyer_offer_unanswered: No: the chat ends on the buyer's lower offer or request for a discount that the seller has not accepted.
criteria.no_rejected: No: the buyer rejected the seller's price, or one side gave up.
criteria.no_never_got_to_price: No: the chat never got to a price, or it is incomplete or nonsensical.
